text.p: Romania's inflation should drop this month from a record of more than 30 percent for March and the government will press ahead with efforts to bring down nominal interest rates, the central bank's chief economist said.

Daniel Daianu told reporters at the annual meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) that the unexpected jump in inflation last month to 30.7 percent from 18.8 percent in February reflected price rises called for under the reform programme.

"Some of the lifting of prices did not take place in February. It took place in March and worsened the figure," Daianu said. "April should be a much better month. "We are already witnessing a lowering of prices," he said. "It could be below 10 percent."
Daianu said lower inflation would help bring down nominal interest rates. "This means being consistent with monetary policy, imposing financial discipline."
